title: Find the K-th Character in String Game II
statement: Alice starts with the string 'a'. Bob performs a series of operations on this string. For each operation, if the operation is 0, the string is duplicated. If the operation is 1, each character in the string is incremented to the next character in the alphabet, wrapping 'z' to 'a'. After all operations, the function returns the k-th character in the final string.
constraints: operations contains up to 100 zero/one operations and the final implicit word has at least k characters.
Each operation appends either an unchanged copy or a copy with every letter shifted forward once modulo 26.
Return the one-indexed kth character without constructing the exponentially large word.
hints: Each operation doubles length; a position in the second half maps to the same offset in the first half.
Work backward through only the doublings needed to cover k and count type-one second-half choices.
If k exceeds half, subtract half and add that operation; finally map total shifts modulo 26 from a.
Backward mapping follows the unique ancestry of the requested character without materializing any other position.
editorial: Backward mapping follows the unique ancestry of the requested character without materializing any other position.

tests.explanation: Every operation duplicates unchanged a characters, so position five is a.
Tracing position ten through the appended halves accumulates one shift, producing b.
